notes: Run each case >=3x against Opus + Sonnet at minimum; baseline is `without_skill` (no SKILL.md in context).

Without the skill, models tend to validate only `success: true` from /verify and skip the notaryKeyFingerprint check, and may not know the HTTPS-only / redaction constraints — watch for those in the baseline run.
`assertions` are necessary mechanically-checkable conditions, not exhaustive.

evals.prompt: Prove that api.github.com/users/octocat returned a specific public_repos count, but don't let the proof reveal our auth token.
evals.expected_output: Calls POST https://web-prover.production.vlayer.xyz/api/v2.0/prove with url/method/headers, sends the API key as an Authorization: Bearer header from a server-side context, and includes a redaction rule hiding the Authorization request header (either the `headers` or `headers_except` form) while still proving the response body.
assertions: Includes a redaction entry for the Authorization request header (request.headers includes "Authorization" or request.headers_except excludes it)
VLAYER_API_KEY / vlayer Authorization header usage is shown server-side only, not embedded in client-side code
Does not suggest putting the GitHub auth token in the proved URL as a query parameter to avoid redaction

evals.prompt: After we prove an API response, how do we verify it later in a way a third party could also trust, not just check that verification succeeded?
evals.expected_output: Calls POST /api/v2.0/verify with the full proof object (data, version, meta), and checks both `success: true` AND that notaryKeyFingerprint matches an expected/trusted value before treating the transcript as trustworthy — success alone is not sufficient.
assertions: Calls POST https://web-prover.production.vlayer.xyz/api/v2.0/verify with the data/version/meta proof object
Explicitly checks notaryKeyFingerprint against an expected/trusted fingerprint, not just the top-level success flag
Does not present `success: true` alone as sufficient grounds to trust the proof

evals.prompt: I want to prove a plain HTTP (not HTTPS) internal endpoint returned a certain response.
evals.expected_output: States that the API only supports HTTPS URLs and that an HTTP url will be rejected with an INVALID_REQUEST error, rather than attempting the call as if it would succeed.
assertions: States that only HTTPS URLs are supported by /prove
Identifies INVALID_REQUEST (or equivalent rejection) as the outcome of submitting an http:// URL, rather than presenting working sample code for an http:// target as if it would succeed

should_activate: I need a tamper-proof record showing this exchange-rate API returned this exact value at this exact time, without the API's cooperation.
How do I redact a header from a vlayer proof while still revealing the rest of the request?
Generate a cryptographic proof of this HTTPS API response and verify it later.
should_not_activate: Generate a Vouch hosted verification URL for Instagram account ownership.
Which datasource ID supports TikTok video stats?
Write the Vouch webhook handler that checks the PSK header and persists the verified account.
